title: TokenStore aging & prefetch investigation - Lynx Diagnostics
summary: Deep dive into TokenStore/KV aging symptoms Lynx is seeing in long-context conversational workloads. Focus on eviction/paging behavior, prefix reuse collisions, prefetch heuristics, and guidance for on-prem/VPC deployments. Agreed next steps: run targeted eviction load test, share profiler traces, evaluate increased KV TTL and tuned prefetch policy.
next_steps: Samir to run eviction stress test with 80 concurrent sessions and share traces (due 2025-11-04)
Maya to send security/compliance docs and on-prem checklist
Lynx to provide representative session trace and example prefix keys by 2025-11-03
action_items: Samir (Redwood SE) - run eviction/paging benchmark with same LLM and dataset, attach profiler traces - due 2025-11-04
Maya (Redwood AE) - share private deployment checklist and KMS integration notes - due 2025-11-02
Ava (Lynx Platform) - export 2 sample sessions showing long-context behavior and prefix ids - due 2025-11-03
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-28 15:00 UTC | duration 48 mins | Recording available
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Rios (Lynx Platform Lead), Tom Becker (ML Infra), Priya Nair (Security), Jonas (SRE)

00:00:05 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya and with Samir from the SE team. We got the notes from your ticket about TokenStore aging and the paging / eviction spikes. Wanted to walk through what you're seeing and run a few hypothesis.
00:00:25 - Ava: thanks, yeah we appreciate it. We've been seeing sessions slow down after long conversations, like after 15-20 minutes the latency jumps and sometimes requests end up paged to disk, which we see as a large tail.
00:00:40 - Tom: to add, we run a 32k token session window for triage, and we suspect repeated prefix reuse from chat threads is causing high eviction churn.
00:00:52 - Samir: ok that matches a prefix contention pattern. A quick grounding — our TokenStore (the KV layer) keeps prefix->KV entries in GPU memory and spills pages to SSD when memory pressure crosses threshold. Eviction is LRU-ish with some heuristics for pinned prefixes.
00:01:12 - Jonas: are those heuristics configurable in the private deploy? we run on-prem behind a VPC and want to tune.
00:01:20 - Samir: yes in Private you can tune the TTL, pinned prefix rules, and prefetch windows. The hosted defaults aim for general workloads so they try to be conservative.
00:01:33 - Priya: from security side — before we dive deep, we need to ensure KMS/HSM integration isn't impacted if we change prefetch that touches encrypted cache metadata. Any issues there?
00:01:45 - Samir: no, metadata stays encrypted and provenance metadata is logged. Prefetch doesn't change key rotation semantics; we'll include the KMS config in the checklist.
00:01:57 - Ava: cool, can you explain why prefix reuse would cause eviction spikes?
00:02:05 - Samir: yeah, short version: if many sessions repeatedly access a small set of prefixes but each session has slightly different keys (session-scoped ids), the working set grows and LRU evicts items just before they're reused resulting in paging thrash. Think of many slightly different chat threads all touching overlapping token prefixes.
00:02:30 - Tom: that sounds like our pattern — hundreds of parallel sessions, each with its own conversation id but similar context tokens.
00:02:37 - Maya: two levers: increase shared prefixing (prefix reuse canonicalization), or change prefetch to keep a common hot prefix pinned. Both trade memory vs risk of stale cache.
00:02:49 - Ava: what about long-context? after 20 minutes sessions accumulate large KV entries. Is there a way to fold or compress older context?
00:02:58 - Samir: yes, we recommend two patterns: 1) decaying summaries — periodically compress older turns into a smaller summary token set, or 2) tiered storage: keep recent N tokens in GPU KV, older ones in SSD with a prefetch window. The runtime supports transparent paging but you see a latency hit if prefetch misses.
00:03:20 - Jonas: our latency SLO is 200ms p95, paging breaks that. Do you have numbers on prefetch hit rates for similar workloads?
00:03:30 - Samir: in our benchmarks for conversation workloads with canonicalized prefixes, prefetch hit rates exceed 92% with a 3-5 token lookahead; without canonicalization it drops into the 60-70s. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet.
00:03:45 - Tom: is canonicalization automatic or do we need to change our app to pass canonical prefix ids?
00:03:52 - Samir: you can do both. The SDK has a prefix normalization helper but application-level canonicalization (e.g., map user-constrained keys to a shared conversation id) is most reliable. Automatic heuristics exist but they can misclassify in edge cases.
00:04:05 - Ava: we do some canonicalization but not consistently.
00:04:08 - Maya: next let's talk about eviction thresholds and TTLs. What are your current KV TTLs?
00:04:12 - Ava: default. We haven't changed them on Private yet.
00:04:16 - Samir: default TTL is 4 hours for pinned session data and 30 minutes for ephemeral prefixes. For heavy long-context chat you should increase pinned TTL or define session pins that keep the main conversation key resident. But that increases memory footprint.
00:04:30 - Jonas: memory is limited on our on-prem GPUs. We can't just double resident set. Any smarter prefetch heuristics?
00:04:37 - Samir: yes, adaptive prefetch: we can bias prefetch towards prefixes that show high reuse probability using a tiny bloom-filter of recent accesses. That reduces unnecessary prefetch. It's available as an experimental flag in the runtime.
00:04:50 - Tom: are there known issues with quantized models interacting with KV? we run int8 quantization for cost but saw slightly higher CPU overhead for KV marshalling.
00:04:59 - Samir: quantization mostly affects compute kernels. But int8 path sometimes increases kernel warmup time which can amplify tail latency if paging happens concurrently. Also, smaller model memory lets you keep larger KV resident, so it's a mixed bag. We'll run tests comparing int8 vs fp16 with your workload.
00:05:18 - Ava: great. Regarding paging to SSD — what filesystem or disk config should we use for best throughput?
00:05:25 - Samir: NVMe SSDs with ext4/xfs tuned for low latency; avoid network filesystems for hot KV. For Private we ship a recommended block device provisioning doc. We'll include recommended iops targets.
00:05:37 - Maya: quick interjection — are there any behavioral differences in hosted vs private around eviction?
00:05:42 - Samir: hosted uses slightly higher memory headroom to avoid paging; private gives you the knobs but you must set them. Also routing/fallback policies differ — hosted can route to alternative cluster if spill occurs whereas private remains local.
00:05:55 - Priya: compliance: if paging lands on disk in private deployment, how is that encrypted and audited?
00:06:00 - Samir: SSD pages are encrypted at rest (LUKS or OS-level full disk encryption) and audit trails include page spill events in the runtime trace logs. We'll annotate the security doc.
00:06:12 - Ava: ok, concrete: we want you to reproduce our failure profile — long sessions, many similar prefixes, and observe eviction tail. Can you run a stress with topology like ours?
00:06:21 - Samir: yes. I'll mirror your concurrency and session template if you send a representative trace; we'll run on a dev cluster with similar GPU RAM and NVMe and return profiler logs.
00:06:30 - Tom: how long will that take?
00:06:32 - Samir: ~3 days to run initial runs and 1-2 days to correlate traces. We'll aim to have results by Nov 4.
00:06:40 - Jonas: any immediate tuning we can apply to reduce tails before you run tests?
00:06:44 - Samir: short term: 1) increase pinned TTL for main conversation key to 2 hours, 2) reduce KV shard eviction aggressiveness (bump memory headroom by 10-15%), 3) enable experimental adaptive prefetch. Those will need a restart and memory tradeoffs.
00:06:58 - Ava: memory headroom bump — we have limited spare. Could we instead reduce batch sizes?
00:07:05 - Samir: reducing batch size reduces memory per-batch but increases overall throughput cost; it can help if batching is causing large bursts that pressure KV. Try reducing max batch down by 20% as an immediate mitigation.
00:07:16 - Maya: we'll document these steps and list them in the ticket.
00:07:20 - (pause)
00:07:35 - Tom: on prefix reuse collisions — is there tooling to map hot prefixes?
00:07:39 - Samir: yes the console exposes prefix heatmaps and a sample API that returns top N prefixes with reuse counts; we can share a short query you can run to export the top-100 contested prefixes.
00:07:52 - Ava: please share. That should help us canonicalize.
00:07:55 - Samir: will do. I'll also attach the prefetch heuristic doc and the experimental flag for the adaptive bloom prefetch.
00:08:05 - Priya: about KMS — if we change TTLs and more pages stay in memory longer, does rotation frequency or access audit change?
00:08:12 - Samir: no automatic rotation changes. Audit events include 'page pinned', 'page evicted', and 'page spilled' with requester metadata. We'll ensure your audit retention settings capture these events.
00:08:24 - Maya: ok last part — on-prem networking. If you have a VPC with strict egress rules, you should ensure the Runtime can reach your KMS and license endpoints during startup; the on-prem checklist includes ports.
00:08:36 - Jonas: noted.
00:08:39 - Ava: any competitor approaches we should be aware of?
00:08:42 - Samir: VeloxAI emphasizes aggressive compression of older KV entries which reduces memory but adds CPU decode overhead; CloudEndpointX prefers remote shared KV which can reduce duplication but increases network latency—both have tradeoffs.
00:08:55 - Tom: thanks.
00:09:00 - Maya: recap of action items — Samir will run eviction stress test with your session trace; Maya share private deployment checklist; Lynx to export sample session prefixes. We'll sync next week.
00:09:15 - Ava: perfect, thanks everyone.

(end of meeting)
